name: Paracetamol
commonly_used_for: Fever and mild to moderate pain
warnings: Do not exceed 4g per day. Avoid alcohol. Use caution in liver disease.

name: Ibuprofen
warnings: Take with food. Avoid in kidney disease, peptic ulcer, or late pregnancy. May increase blood pressure.

name: Amoxicillin
commonly_used_for: Bacterial infections (ear, throat, chest, urinary tract)
warnings: Complete the full course. Inform doctor of penicillin allergy. May cause diarrhoea.

name: Metformin
warnings: Take with meals to reduce stomach upset. Avoid alcohol. Stop before contrast dye procedures.

name: Atorvastatin
commonly_used_for: High cholesterol and prevention of heart disease
warnings: Report unexplained muscle pain immediately. Avoid grapefruit juice. Inform doctor if pregnant.

name: Amlodipine
commonly_used_for: High blood pressure and chest pain (angina)
warnings: May cause ankle swelling and flushing. Do not stop suddenly without doctor advice.

name: Omeprazole
warnings: Take 30 minutes before eating. Long-term use may reduce magnesium and B12 levels.

name: Cetirizine
warnings: May cause drowsiness. Avoid driving until you know how it affects you. Avoid alcohol.

name: Azithromycin
typical_dosage: 500mg once daily for 3 days (or as directed)
warnings: Complete the full course. May cause stomach upset. Rare risk of abnormal heart rhythm.

name: Losartan
commonly_used_for: High blood pressure and kidney protection in diabetes
warnings: Avoid potassium supplements unless directed. Do not use in pregnancy. Monitor kidney function.

name: Pantoprazole
warnings: Take before meals. Long-term use may affect bone density and magnesium levels.

name: Metronidazole
commonly_used_for: Bacterial and parasitic infections (gut, dental, skin)
warnings: Avoid alcohol during treatment and for 48 hours after. May cause metallic taste.

name: Doxycycline
warnings: Take with a full glass of water. Avoid lying down for 30 minutes after. Increases sun sensitivity.

name: Prednisolone
typical_dosage: As directed by doctor (dose varies widely)
warnings: Do not stop suddenly — taper as directed. May raise blood sugar and blood pressure. Take with food.

name: Salbutamol
warnings: Shake inhaler before use. Rinse mouth after inhaled doses. Overuse may cause tremor and fast heartbeat.

name: Glimepiride
warnings: Take with food. Watch for signs of low blood sugar. Avoid skipping meals.

name: Clopidogrel
commonly_used_for: Prevention of heart attack and stroke (blood thinner)
warnings: Inform all doctors before surgery. Do not stop without consulting your doctor. May increase bleeding risk.

name: Levothyroxine
typical_dosage: 25mcg–200mcg once daily on an empty stomach
warnings: Take 30–60 minutes before breakfast. Do not take with calcium, iron, or antacids. Regular blood tests needed.

name: Ciprofloxacin
commonly_used_for: Urinary tract, respiratory, skin, and eye infections
warnings: Take with plenty of water. Avoid antacids within 2 hours. May cause tendon problems in elderly.

name: Ranitidine
warnings: Take as directed. May interact with other medicines. Some formulations withdrawn in certain countries — check availability.

name: Diclofenac
typical_dosage: 50mg two to three times daily with food
warnings: Take with food. Avoid in heart, kidney, or stomach ulcer conditions.

name: Aspirin
commonly_used_for: Pain relief, fever, and blood thinning (low dose)
warnings: Avoid in children with viral infections (Reye's syndrome risk). Take with food. Increases bleeding risk.

name: Combiflam
typical_dosage: 1 tablet up to 3 times daily after food
warnings: Take after food. Avoid prolonged use without medical advice.

name: Norfloxacin
warnings: Take on an empty stomach. Avoid antacids within 2 hours. Increases sun sensitivity.

name: Digene
typical_dosage: 1–2 tablets or 10ml as needed after meals
warnings: Do not take with other medicines within 2 hours. Avoid frequent long-term use without advice.

name: Fexofenadine
commonly_used_for: Allergy relief (less drowsy than older antihistamines)
warnings: Avoid taking with fruit juices (may reduce absorption). Generally non-drowsy but individual response varies.

name: Levocetirizine
warnings: May cause mild drowsiness in some people. Avoid alcohol.

name: Pheniramine
warnings: Causes significant drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery.

name: Ondansetron
warnings: May cause headache and constipation. Inform doctor of heart rhythm issues.

name: Domperidone
warnings: Take before meals. Avoid in heart rhythm disorders. Limit duration of use.

name: Loperamide
typical_dosage: 4mg initially then 2mg after each loose stool (max 16mg/day)
warnings: Do not use if fever or blood in stool present. Stay hydrated with ORS.

name: ORS
typical_dosage: One sachet dissolved in 1 litre water; sip through the day
commonly_used_for: Dehydration from diarrhoea, vomiting, or heat
warnings: Use clean water to prepare. Discard prepared solution after 24 hours. Seek medical help if symptoms are severe.

name: Dicyclomine
warnings: Avoid in glaucoma or urinary retention. Take before meals if advised.

name: Amitriptyline
commonly_used_for: Nerve pain, migraine prevention, sometimes depression
warnings: Do not stop suddenly. May cause drowsiness and dry mouth. Avoid alcohol.

name: Sertraline
warnings: Do not stop suddenly. Effects may take 2–4 weeks to appear. Discuss all other medicines with your doctor.

name: Alprazolam
warnings: Habit-forming — use only as prescribed. Avoid alcohol. Do not stop abruptly.

name: Montelukast
warnings: Not for immediate asthma attack relief. Take regularly as prescribed even if feeling well.

name: Ambroxol
warnings: Drink plenty of fluids. Generally well tolerated.

name: Dextromethorphan
warnings: Avoid combining with other cough or cold products containing the same ingredient. Avoid in children under 4.

name: Multivitamin
warnings: Do not exceed recommended dose. Consult doctor if pregnant or on other supplements.

name: Calcium Vitamin D3
warnings: Take with food. Avoid excess intake — may affect kidney function over time.

name: Iron Folic Acid
warnings: May cause constipation and dark stools (normal). Take with vitamin C for better absorption.

name: Biotin
commonly_used_for: Hair, skin, and nail health supplement
warnings: Generally safe. Discontinue if unusual skin reactions occur.

name: B-Complex
warnings: Generally safe. Excess long-term doses rarely may cause nerve tingling.

name: Zinc Sulphate
commonly_used_for: Zinc deficiency, immune support, diarrhoea recovery in children
warnings: Take with food to reduce stomach upset. Avoid exceeding recommended dose.

name: Betadine
typical_dosage: Apply to affected area 2–3 times daily
warnings: For external use only. Avoid in thyroid disorders unless advised. Discontinue if irritation occurs.

name: Volini
typical_dosage: Apply to affected area 3–4 times daily
warnings: For external use only. Avoid broken skin. Wash hands after application.

name: Moov
typical_dosage: Apply to affected area as needed
warnings: For external use only. Avoid contact with eyes and broken skin.

name: Telmisartan
warnings: Avoid in pregnancy. Monitor kidney function periodically. May cause dizziness initially.

name: Ramipril
commonly_used_for: High blood pressure and heart protection
warnings: May cause persistent dry cough. Avoid in pregnancy. Monitor kidney function.

name: Atenolol
commonly_used_for: High blood pressure and heart rhythm control
warnings: Do not stop suddenly. May cause fatigue and cold hands or feet. Avoid in asthma.

name: Furosemide
commonly_used_for: Fluid retention and high blood pressure
warnings: Take earlier in the day to avoid night-time urination. Monitor potassium levels.

name: Spironolactone
commonly_used_for: Fluid retention and heart failure management
warnings: Monitor potassium levels. Avoid potassium supplements unless directed.

name: Glipizide
warnings: Take before meals. Watch for signs of low blood sugar.

name: Sitagliptin
warnings: Generally well tolerated. Inform doctor of pancreas-related conditions.

name: Rosuvastatin
warnings: Report unexplained muscle pain. Avoid excess alcohol. Periodic liver function tests advised.

name: Clonazepam
warnings: Habit-forming — use only as prescribed. Avoid alcohol. Do not stop abruptly.

name: Escitalopram
warnings: Do not stop suddenly. Effects may take 2–4 weeks. Avoid alcohol.

name: Diazepam
warnings: Habit-forming — use only as prescribed. Causes drowsiness. Avoid alcohol and driving.

name: Hydrochlorothiazide
commonly_used_for: High blood pressure and fluid retention
warnings: Monitor electrolyte levels. May increase blood sugar and uric acid slightly.

name: Clindamycin
typical_dosage: 150mg–450mg every 6 hours (oral) or apply twice daily (topical)
warnings: Complete full oral course. May cause diarrhoea — report severe or bloody diarrhoea immediately.

name: Fluconazole
commonly_used_for: Fungal infections including vaginal yeast infections
warnings: May interact with several other medicines — inform your doctor of all medications.

name: Clotrimazole
warnings: For external use only unless prescribed otherwise. Complete the full duration even if symptoms improve.

name: Mupirocin
warnings: For external use only. Avoid contact with eyes.

name: Betamethasone
typical_dosage: Apply thin layer once or twice daily
warnings: Avoid prolonged use on face or thin skin. Do not use on infected skin without antibiotic cover.

name: Calamine Lotion
typical_dosage: Apply to affected area as needed
warnings: For external use only. Discontinue if irritation worsens.

name: Hydroxyzine
warnings: Causes drowsiness. Avoid alcohol and driving.

name: Rabeprazole
warnings: Take before meals. Long-term use may affect bone density and magnesium levels.

name: Sucralfate
typical_dosage: 1g four times daily on empty stomach
warnings: Take on an empty stomach at least 1 hour before meals. Avoid taking with antacids simultaneously.

name: Simethicone
warnings: Generally very safe. No major interactions.

name: Mefenamic Acid
warnings: Take after food. Avoid in stomach ulcer or kidney disease.

name: Tranexamic Acid
commonly_used_for: Heavy menstrual bleeding and controlling bleeding
warnings: Avoid in history of blood clots unless directed by doctor.

name: Folic Acid
typical_dosage: 5mg once daily (or as directed in pregnancy)
warnings: Generally very safe. Important during pregnancy for neural tube development.

name: Vitamin D3
warnings: Take as directed by blood test results. Avoid excess unsupervised intake.

name: Methylcobalamin
commonly_used_for: Vitamin B12 deficiency and nerve health
warnings: Generally very safe. Long-term deficiency needs monitoring even after starting treatment.

name: Ivermectin
typical_dosage: Dose based on body weight (single or repeat dose as directed)
warnings: Take on empty stomach as directed. Avoid in pregnancy unless directed.

name: Permethrin
typical_dosage: Apply to entire body, wash off after 8–14 hours
warnings: Follow application instructions exactly. Avoid contact with eyes and mouth.

name: Chlorhexidine
commonly_used_for: Gum disease, mouth ulcers, dental infections
warnings: Do not swallow. May cause temporary staining of teeth with prolonged use.

name: Benzoyl Peroxide
warnings: May cause dryness and mild irritation initially. Avoid sun exposure without sunscreen.

name: Adapalene
warnings: May cause initial dryness and peeling. Use sunscreen during the day.

name: Loratadine
warnings: Generally non-drowsy. Avoid exceeding recommended dose.

name: Chlorpheniramine
warnings: Causes drowsiness. Avoid alcohol and driving.

name: Terbutaline
warnings: May cause tremor and rapid heartbeat. Use as directed.

name: Budesonide
typical_dosage: As directed (varies by strength and condition)
warnings: Rinse mouth after use to prevent oral thrush. Not for immediate attack relief.

name: Ipratropium
typical_dosage: 2 puffs three to four times daily
warnings: Avoid spraying near eyes. Effects are gradual, not for sudden attacks.

name: Naproxen
warnings: Take with food. Avoid in kidney disease or stomach ulcer history.

name: Etoricoxib
warnings: Avoid in heart disease. Take with food if stomach upset occurs.

name: Tramadol
warnings: Habit-forming with prolonged use. May cause drowsiness and nausea. Avoid alcohol.
